quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: A motorcycle horn:

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.

questions.explanation: A horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: A helmet will not give the best protection if it:
questions.explanation: A helmet must meet DOT standards and fit snugly to protect you best. It should have no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press the front brake and jam the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: To brake, squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Use both brakes when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is usually:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Should not puff up when riding.
Are not needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not puff up when riding.
questions.explanation: Good motorcycle rain suits will not tear or puff up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left part of your lane.
Ride in the right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: If you follow a car, stay in the center of your lane. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Before riding, check your tires for all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Help you be seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position should help you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane from other drivers, shows your intentions, and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: To be seen better at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Keeping your headlight on is the most important thing you can do to help others see you at an intersection. Always ride with your headlight on.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Slow down by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by closing the throttle gradually. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can and fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: Which item provides the best protection for a rider?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that won't shatter protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection as goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: They may help other drivers see you.
They do not help improve visibility.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Choosing a brightly-colored helmet is recommended. The helmet protects you in a crash. The bright color also helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can block your side vision.
They allow you to see to the sides as needed for safe riding.
You don't have to wear one if it limits your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They allow you to see to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Some people worry that helmets limit side vision, but this is not true. Approved helmets let you see to the sides as much as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track often works best, but it depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or more is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: What is true about a plastic face shield that won't shatter?

options.text: It can protect your face in a crash.
It only protects you from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
You should not use it with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield that won't shatter protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of sturdy material, boots or shoes that are high and cover your ankles, and gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What is recommended for a motorcyclist?

options.text: Use the brake throughout the turn.

questions.explanation: You should change gears before you enter a turn.
